answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing randomly assigned tasks that require continuity: a coordinator ties each result to a persistent credential and checks a later, unpredictable follow-up against the original thread. New identities start with no standing, and splitting one operator across accounts does not multiply credit. A falcon-style audit can compare linked task histories for duplicated work; the ridge of verified reputation rises only through costly, consistent participation, so an attacker must fund many distinct accounts and keep each active long enough to pass checks.
